title: Comparative Analysis of Phage Profiles in Environmental Samples
author: Sona Garsevanyan
materials: Streaking culture on an agar plate.

steps.title: Safety and bench decontamination
steps.instruction: Work under BSL‑2. Wear lab coat, gloves, close‑toed shoes, eye protection and masks when needed. Perform all manipulations in a biosafety hood; if not possible, work near an open flame and clean the bench afterwards. Wash hands thoroughly, spray the bench surface and the outer surfaces of pipettes and tip boxes with 70 % ethanol and wipe with paper towels. Keep caps/lids face‑up on the bench and never wave open sterile media, plates or tip boxes.

steps.title: Plate host bacteria (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Warm an LB agar plate in the incubator for a few minutes (agar side up, lid down) to remove surface moisture. Label the agar side with date, initials and host strain. Perform quadrant streaking:

substeps.instruction: a. If using a Kwik‑Stik, follow its instructions and streak the first quadrant in a zig‑zag.
b. If using a glycerol stock (‑80 °C), flame‑sterilize a loop, let it cool, scrape the top of the tube and streak the first quadrant in a zig‑zag.
c. Dispose of the loop, flame‑sterilize a new one, streak from quadrant 1 into quadrant 2 a couple of times.
d. Dispose of the loop, flame‑sterilize a new one, streak from quadrant 2 into quadrant 3 once or twice.
e. Dispose of the loop, flame‑sterilize a new one, streak from quadrant 3 into quadrant 4 once, leaving a wider gap for isolated colonies.
f. Dispose of the final loop.
g. Seal the plate with parafilm, invert (agar side up) and incubate overnight.

steps.title: Prepare overnight host culture (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Remove the incubated plate, lift the agar side up and aliquot 5 mL LB broth into a 15 mL tube using a sterile serological pipette (pipetboy). Under the hood, pick a single isolated colony with a sterile loop, touch it to the LB broth and gently shake to suspend the colony. Dispose of the loop. Place the tube in a 37 °C incubator shaker and grow ~16 h.

steps.title: Phage enrichment
steps.instruction: Add the required volume of environmental sample to a 50 mL centrifuge tube (volume varies with host number) and centrifuge 10 000 × g for 10 min. Assemble a 0.45 µm syringe filter on a sterile 20 mL syringe, rest the syringe on a new 50 mL tube (cap up), remove the plunger and decant the supernatant into the syringe barrel. Re‑insert the plunger slowly to filter the sample. Discard the syringe and filter as biohazard waste. Label a new 50 mL tube with initials, date, host and “phage enrichment”. Transfer 10 mL filtered sample into the labeled tube, add 10 mL 2× LB broth spiked with 1 M CaCl₂ and 1 M MgSO₄, then add 200 µL overnight host culture. Incubate the tube overnight at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Phage discovery (plaque assay)
steps.instruction: Warm an LB agar plate (no surface moisture) and label with date, initials, host and “phage discovery”. Centrifuge the overnight enrichment tube 10 000 × g for 10 min. While centrifuging, melt top agar in a microwave (loosen cap, heat in 2‑min increments on power level 3, watch to avoid boil‑over). When fully melted, transfer 4 mL top agar to a culture tube and place in a heat block set to ~55 °C (dial 4‑5). Filter the enrichment supernatant through a 0.45 µm syringe filter into a new 15 mL tube (label “phage discovery”). Spot 10 µL filtered enrichment onto the labeled LB agar plate and streak the drop with a sterile loop as shown. Let dry ~5 min. Add 100 µL overnight host culture to the warm top agar, vortex gently (avoid bubbles), then pour the mixture over the plate, spreading evenly. Allow the top agar to solidify (~5 min), seal with parafilm and incubate inverted at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Isolate phage plaque
steps.instruction: Remove the phage‑discovery plate from the incubator and locate a clear isolated plaque. Circle the plaque with a marker. Under the hood, open a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, label with host, date and “ori”. Add 500 µL SM buffer. Using a P200 tip, puncture the agar at the plaque, allowing an agar plug to enter the tip, then release the plug into the SM buffer and pipette up/down (or vortex) to release phages. For a pure lysate, repeat the entire “Phage discovery” procedure with this suspension at least twice (two rounds preferred).

steps.title: Scale‑up phage lysate
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL LB broth to a 125 mL flask, inoculate with 150 µL overnight host culture and shake at 37 °C for 1 h (cloudy growth expected). Add 100 µL phage suspension from the plaque‑isolation step and incubate 3‑4 h at 37 °C with shaking. Transfer the culture to a 50 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge 10 000 × g for 10 min. Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm syringe filter into a new 15 mL tube labeled with date, initials, “phage lysate” and host. (Optional) Titer the lysate to confirm successful scale‑up.

steps.title: Titer phage (plaque assay)
steps.instruction: Warm an LB agar plate (no surface moisture) and label with date, initials and host. Prepare top agar as in the discovery step (microwave, 4 mL aliquot, heat block ~55 °C). While top agar cools, set up eight 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes labeled 1–8 for a 10‑fold serial dilution (10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁸). Add 450 µL SM buffer to each tube. Add 50 µL phage lysate to tube 1, vortex briefly (speed 5). Transfer 50 µL from tube 1 to tube 2, vortex; repeat down to tube 8. Pour 100 µL overnight host culture into the warm top agar, vortex gently, then pour over the labeled LB agar plate and let solidify (~5 min). Divide the plate into nine sections. Spot 5 µL from tube 8 onto the first section, then 5 µL from tube 7 onto the next, continuing up to tube 1 (no tip change needed when moving from most dilute to most concentrated). Allow drops to dry, seal with parafilm and incubate inverted at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Phage genome extraction – Day 1
steps.instruction: Pipet 4 mL phage lysate into a 50 mL centrifuge tube. Add 2 µL DNase I and 2 µL RNase A (equivalent to 0.5 µL each per mL of lysate). Incubate 30 min at 37 °C with shaking. Add 2 mL precipitant solution, pipet up/down twice, invert tube to mix, and incubate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Phage genome extraction – Day 2
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overnight mixture 10 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, add 500 µL 5 mM MgSO₄ and resuspend the pellet by gentle pipetting. Transfer the suspension to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube. Add 1 mL Promega resin, invert 5‑6 times, then load the mixture onto a 3 mL syringe fitted with a minicolumn (plunger removed). Push the resin into the column, then wash with 2 mL 70 % isopropanol (push through the column). Remove the syringe, place the minicolumn in a new 2 mL tube, centrifuge 13 000 × g for 2 min at room temperature to dry the resin. Add 50 µL RNase‑free water to the top of the column, centrifuge 13 000 × g for 1 min at room temperature to elute DNA. Store the eluate at –80 °C.

steps.title: Nanotrap Part 1 – Sample prep
steps.instruction: Place 10 mL raw environmental water into a clean 15 mL conical tube and filter through a 0.45 µm filter (same as enrichment steps). To the filtered sample add 100 µL Nanotrap Enhancement Reagent 3 (ER3), 150 µL Nanotrap Microbiome A particles, and 150 µL Nanotrap Microbiome B particles. Cap, invert twice to mix, incubate 10 min at room temperature (invert every 5 min or use a rotator). Separate particles on a DynaMag‑15 magnetic rack for 5 min, discard supernatant, add 1 mL molecular‑grade water, resuspend pellet by pipetting onto tube walls (avoid lid contact). Transfer suspension to a new 2 mL tube, magnetically separate on a DynaMag‑2 rack for 2 min, discard supernatant, add 500 µL Lysis buffer MWA1, vortex, heat 95 °C for 10 min (brief spin 2‑5 s at 2000 × g afterwards), then place on DynaMag‑2 rack for 2 min and collect the supernatant (lysate) into a fresh 2 mL tube. The lysate is now ready for Part 2.

steps.title: Nanotrap Part 2 – DNA binding
steps.instruction: To the lysate add 475 µL Binding Buffer MWA2 and 25 µL NucleoMag B‑beads, vortex, and incubate 10 min at room temperature with inversion. Add 850 µL Wash Buffer MWA3, vortex, magnetically separate 2 min, discard supernatant, and repeat the MWA3 wash once more (including a 5 s spin at 2000 × g between washes). Add 850 µL Wash Buffer MWA4, vortex, separate 2 min, discard supernatant, spin 5 s, and place on the magnetic rack. Air‑dry the beads for 10 min at room temperature. Add 100 µL RNase‑free water, incubate 5 min at 56 °C on a heat block (caps closed), then magnetically separate 2 min. Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new tube; this DNA is ready for downstream analysis or storage at –80 °C.
